cultural.vision_reason: This is a carved wooden kachina doll depicting a Mudhead Clown figure (Koshare-type), a well-documented Hopi ritual/ceremonial carving tradition, matching the museum's detailed description of the mask, protuberances, and dance attire.

physical.title: kachina-doll
physical.summary: Kachina-doll; carved of wood; in the form of Mud Head Clown; circle of wood for base; kachina stands on base on right foot, left foot raised behind, arms outstretched; wears case mask on head with round protruberance on either side and one on back, pointed protruberance out top, all decorated with feathers; eyes and mouth protrude from front; painted reddish-brown with white markings, black circle outlined in white with white dots on stomach; beige leather scarf around neck; black vinyl skirt with green and red stripe along bottom; white leather sash decorated with turquoise flowers around waist; beige leather bands on upper arms and wrists and around knees; lower arms and lower legs painted black with white spots; socks painted black, boots white; holds wood drum with leather skins in left hand, wooden drumstick with end covered with leather in right hand; red cotton blanket roll hanging from black wool strap around left shoulder; "Twakkoyem Mudhead" written on bottom.
